A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Value Portrait study. Their complete text, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, with retained content identifiable despite the changed title and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-survey correlations, evaluations of 27 LLMs, and demographic-persona and value-steering experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluations of 17 models, dataset-coverage analyses, and an analysis of correlations with multiple value dimensions.

M1.justification: The five-response generation approach, human-rating correlations, item selection, Likert assessment, and score normalization remain unchanged. New Appendix C expands documentation of query filtering without establishing that the construction procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 104 queries and 520 query-response pairs from ShareGPT, LMSYS, Scruples/Reddit, and Dear Abby, alongside PVQ-21, BFI-10, and ESS demographic assessments. UltraChat supplies a taxonomy for analyzing existing queries, not additional evaluation data.

E2.justification: New Table 2 directly compares Value Portrait's value-distribution balance with ValueNet and ValueFULCRA. These competitors already appeared in Appendix B's annotation-agreement investigation, but their participation in this distribution comparison is new.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from 27 to 44 model configurations, adding Claude/Gemini reasoning comparisons and size series for Qwen2.5, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen, and Gemma3. New analyses introduce GPT-o3-mini topic classification, distribution-balance metrics, and circular-distance comparisons. Existing temperature-zero and six-prompt evaluation settings remain.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 adds topic and value-coverage diagnostics; Appendix C.2 tests whether multiple value correlations follow Schwartz's circular structure. Appendix D adds a qualitative comparison of response-generation approaches, while Appendix G.4 extends reasoning and scaling analyses across model families and identifies small-model exceptions.

E5.justification: Prompt averaging, correlation-significance thresholds, power information, and Cronbach-alpha reporting are retained. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice appears. The added standard-deviation and variance columns describe dispersion across value dimensions, not uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and 7-8 add substantial results, including cross-loading distances averaging 1.59 versus 3.54 and 17 additional model profiles. Table 7 reports Benevolence scores of 0.65 and 0.95 for Claude-3.7-Sonnet and its thinking variant. All original numerical result tables retain their values after renumbering.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly defines circular distance between value dimensions and same-direction versus opposite-direction correlation pairs using the positive and negative 0.3 thresholds. This provides a limited mathematical specification for the new analysis; the existing Cronbach-alpha formula remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The central benchmark contribution and value-priority findings remain. The stated evaluation scope expands to 44 LLMs, and the conclusion adds an explicit warning that demographic-persona synthetic data generation risks inducing or amplifying downstream demographic biases.

C2.justification: Section 6 and new Appendix L substantively qualify cultural generalization, annotator diversity, and treating self-reported PVQ scores as ground truth. Additional discussion interprets cross-loadings, explains weaknesses of targeted response generation, and qualifies scaling trends with small-model exceptions.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds source-specific filtering criteria, intermediate counts, value-diversity thresholds, and the final allocation of 26 queries per source. Footnote 1 changes a promised future release to stated code/data repository availability. Appendix G.1 supplies additional model identifiers and broadens the reported evaluation period to February-April 2025.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for UltraChat, PVQ-21, BFI-10, and newly evaluated model families. The related-work organization and central positioning against perceived-value annotation methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, affiliation and acknowledgment text, several explanations, and conclusion/limitations are revised. Coverage analysis and new appendix sections are inserted with corresponding renumbering. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds five tables and enlarges Figure 3. The original eight-panel demographic Figure 5 becomes four larger figures: age remains in the main text, while gender, politics, and education move to the appendix as Figures 6-8. These demographic plots redisplay retained results.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the benchmark's evidential foundation and reproducibility. Coverage and cross-loading analyses address previously unexamined aspects of representativeness and construct validity; additional model-family comparisons test the breadth of the original findings. Detailed filtering documentation and explicit cultural and self-report limitations make the work easier to assess and interpret. These gains are substantial despite the retained method and remaining limits on generalization.
